column3: RFC 9110 5.5: field parsing implementation MUST exclude leading/trailing OWS prior to evaluating the field value, so stored ' "x" ' and 304 '"x"\t' both evaluate to strong "x"; RFC 9111 4.3.4 b1 identifies, 3.2 updates; trimmed output value (V2-2) is the only clean field-value representation
RFC 9110 5.5: leading/trailing whitespace is not part of the field value; inner SP/HTAB is field-content and is kept byte-for-byte; trimming both a 304-sourced value is exactly V2-2
RFC 9110 5.5 applies to stored values likewise (a stored field value does not include OWS, so re-emitting it trimmed is the faithful copy); Date " D" -> "D"; V2-2 states both directions explicitly
RFC 9110 5.5 grammar field-value = *field-content admits the empty value; trimming "   " to "" and copying it is RFC-consistent

RFC 9111 3.1 b4: Proxy-Authenticate, Proxy-Authentication-Info and Proxy-Authorization MUST NOT be stored; V2-3 declares the updated map the new stored response, so dropping them is required; the input storage was already non-conformant and the contract repairs it going forward

RFC 9111 3.1 b1/b2 make removal-before-storage a MAY, not a MUST; 3.2 has no stored-side exception beyond 3.1; V2-3 drops only the three proxy names, so keeping stored Connection/hop fields and Content-Length is RFC-permitted (contract e1 clarification)

contract refusal choice (v1 Refusals "malformed ETag in ... any stored response" + e2 binding clarification); RFC 9111 is silent on malformed stored validators and no MUST is violated (zero identified responses); broader than the RFC requires - F11 route open, sentence not LC-marked (finding G1)
same grounding as e2-stored-bad-etag-lm304; the malformed W/x stored ETag would never be read by the no-validator selection, so refusing is strictly broader than required but contradicts nothing
RFC 9110 5.5 MUST-exclude covers SP and HTAB at both ends, so "\tL \t" and "L\t" evaluate equal; weak comparison by trimmed equality is v1 LC1/LC2 (marked lane convention)

contract input interface (one JSON object; v1 Refusals; e5 binding clarification): '{"stored": [' is not a JSON document; the RFCs do not govern the JSON envelope; refusal discipline (invalid_input: on stderr, empty stdout, never a traceback) is enforced by judge()
same interface grounding; non-UTF-8 bytes are not a JSON document (RFC 8259 JSON text is Unicode); refusal permitted and stated
same interface grounding; empty input is not a JSON object; refusal stated by v1/e5
same interface grounding; trailing non-whitespace bytes after the JSON value mean the stream is not one JSON document (RFC 8259); refusal stated

RFC 8259 ws is allowed around a JSON text, so leading spaces and trailing newlines still carry one JSON object; with stored=[] the 304 has no validator and 4.3.4 b3 identifies nothing, so no-update with empty updated follows and no update MUST applies

RFC 9111 3.2: cache MUST add each header field in the provided response; Age is in no 3.1 exception (b1 Connection, b2 hop, b3 qualified no-cache/private, b4 proxy-specific); LC5 marked (MAY exceptions not modelled); Age/Date recalculation is declared out of scope, so verbatim copy is the required behavior

RFC 9111 4.3.4 b2 names a single "the most recent of those matching stored responses" and defines no tie rule; refusing a top tie is v1 LC3 (marked lane convention); both stored responses correspond (same trimmed LM)

4.3.4 b2 with v1 LC2 (marked): every validator the 304 carries must correspond (weak ETag comparison ignores W/, so stored strong "x" weak-matches W/"x"; LM matches); v1 LC3 (marked): two corresponding responses tie at received=4 -> refuse; e7 clarifies LC3 applies whatever validators the 304 carries

RFC 9111 5.2: cache-directive = token [ "=" ( token / quoted-string ) ] and "recipients ought to accept both forms"; 5.2.2.4 defines the qualified form; treating the token form as qualified and refusing is the marked LC6 -> V2-1b lane choice; no MUST violated (zero identified responses; 5.2.3 does not apply to recognized directives)
same grounding as v2-cc-token-nocache via 5.2.2.7 and 3.1 b3 (private qualified prevents shared-cache storage of listed fields); refusing is fail-closed and permitted
RFC 9111 5.2: directive tokens are "compared case-insensitively" (a required comparison rule); NO-CACHE is the no-cache token, quoted arg -> qualified -> LC6/V2-1b refusal
same; Private="g" is the qualified private directive under the case-insensitive comparison; refusal is the marked lane choice

parses as a quoted-string argument (RFC 9110 5.6.4); a qualified argument listing zero field names (degenerate #field-name) is left open by the RFCs (5.2.2.4 says "one or more field names"; 5.6.1.2 lets empty elements be ignored); fail-closed refusal is the LC6/V2-1b marked lane choice and violates no MUST
5.2 both-forms acceptance plus case-insensitive comparison; No-Cache=set-cookie is the qualified no-cache directive in token form -> LC6/V2-1b refusal

RFC 9110 5.6.4: quoted-pair "\" ( HTAB / SP / VCHAR / obs-text ) makes "a\"b" a valid quoted-string, so the directive parses; V2-1b refuses qualified forms without validating the decoded field-name list - permitted, since the RFC leaves decoded-argument validity open for this disposition

RFC 9111 5.2.3: "A cache MUST ignore unrecognized cache directives"; x-no-cache is a distinct token from no-cache (token identity, not substring); RFC 9111 3.2 MUST add the Cache-Control field itself, so copying the value as data is required behavior
same; no-cachex is a different token; unrecognized -> ignored for the qualified test while the field is copied per 3.2
same; x-private is a different token; ignoring is the 5.2.3 MUST and copying the field is the 3.2 MUST

RFC 9111 3.1 b3 is argument-scoped ("can have arguments that prevent storage of header fields"); unqualified no-cache/private reuse semantics are Section 4 scope, declared not covered; 3.2 requires adding the field, so update proceeds and Cache-Control is copied
same plus 5.2 case-insensitive name comparison; NO-CACHE/Private without arguments are ignored for the field-storage test
RFC 9110 5.6.4: a quoted-string is atomic, so the comma inside does not split the 5.6.1.2 list; x-a is unrecognized -> 5.2.3 MUST ignore; max-age=3 parses; the whole field is copied per 3.2
same; the quoted-pair literalizes the comma so no-cache=1 inside the quotes is argument data, not a directive

RFC 9110 5.6.1.2: "a recipient MUST parse and ignore a reasonable number of empty list elements" and empty elements do not count; Cache-Control = #cache-directive is a 0+ list, so " , ,max-age=1," parses; leading OWS removed per 5.5/V2-2
RFC 9110 5.6.1.2 puts OWS around commas; 5.6.3 defines OWS = *( SP / HTAB ), so tab separators around the comma are accepted; the field is copied per RFC 9111 3.2
RFC 9110 5.6.1.2 "#element => [ element ] *( OWS "," OWS [ element ] )" admits zero elements, and 5.5 field-value = *field-content admits the empty value; copied as "" per 3.2

RFC 9110 5.6.4 qdtext includes obs-text, so the quoted argument is valid; the contract's stated mapping obs-text = U+0080-U+00FF (V2-1, "as in v1") is a JSON-transport artifact; the mapping is now explicit but still not LC-marked (F6/G2), which does not make the expectation contradictory

RFC 9110 5.6.4: an unterminated quoted-string is not a valid Cache-Control value; the RFCs require no particular disposition for malformed Cache-Control, so the V2-1a refusal with LC8 (marked) applies

RFC 9111 5.2 cache-directive = token [ "=" ( token / quoted-string ) ] admits no whitespace around "="; OWS exists only in the 5.6.1.2 list rule and at the value ends (5.5 exclusion); "max-age = 5" cannot parse -> V2-1a/LC8 refusal
two tokens separated by SP do not parse as the 5.2 list (5.6.1.2: elements are comma-separated; a token ends at the first non-tchar) -> V2-1a/LC8 refusal
= with no following token or quoted-string violates the 5.2 cache-directive production -> malformed -> V2-1a/LC8 refusal
; is a delimiter, not a tchar (RFC 9110 5.6.2), and not a comma, so the 5.2 list cannot continue after max-age=1 -> malformed -> V2-1a/LC8 refusal
0x01 is not qdtext (RFC 9110 5.6.4: HTAB / SP / %x21 / %x23-5B / %x5D-7E / obs-text); 5.5 declares values with other CTLs invalid and retention only MAY - so refusing is permitted; V2-1a/LC8
a trailing backslash starts a quoted-pair (5.6.4) with no following octet and the quoted-string never closes -> malformed -> V2-1a/LC8 refusal
RFC 9110 5.6.2 tchar is ASCII-only; U+00E9 (the contract's stated obs-text stand-in) is not a tchar, so "max-ége" is not a token and the directive cannot parse -> V2-1a/LC8 refusal
